title: Decision Workspace
pitch: An adaptive WebMCP workspace where agents ask one question at a time, expose trade-offs, and help people reach transparent, grounded decisions.
about_excerpt: An adaptive WebMCP workspace where agents ask one question at a time, expose trade-offs, and help people reach transparent, grounded decisions. Like Comment Story Updates Inspiration Important decisions often get buried in long AI chats. Criteria drift, assumptions disappear, and it becomes hard to tell why a recommendation changed. We wanted a shared workspace where a person can see the decision model evolve instead of receiving an opaque answer. What we built Decision Workspace is a local-first decision canvas for humans and browser agents. It keeps options, weighted criteria, score-and-confidence assessments, evidence, uncertainties, constraints, and recommendations in one inspectable state. The app exposes workflow-level WebMCP tools through navigator.modelContext. An agent can read the current workspace, ask one high-value interview question at a time, process an answer atomically, apply only grounded mappings, and adapt the next question to the new context. Free-text or uncertain answers remain explicitly unresolved instead of being forced into a score. Users can explore temporary what-if scenarios without changing saved state. When the model is sufficiently grounded, the agent can create a readiness-checked Decision Brief with the leading option, drivers, remaining unknowns, and next verification action. The person remains in control of the final decision. How we built it We built the UI with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. The canonical decision store is shared by the UI and the WebMCP adapter, so tool writes are immediately visible in the page and persisted locally on the device. Revision-aware writes and explicit question lifecycle states keep the interview consistent and auditable. Challenges and what we learned The hardest part was designing a small, coherent tool surface instead of exposing every UI control. We learned that an agent workflow needs explicit state reads, deterministic mapping policies, uncertainty preservation, non-destructive scenarios, and readiness gating. WebMCP works best when the browser page is the shared source of truth and the agent changes it through semantic workflow actions. Built With local-first next.js react tailwind typescript vercel webmcp Try it out decision-workspace.vercel.app github.com Submitted to The WebMCP Challenge Created by I originated the product concept and led the end-to-end build of Decision Workspace. I designed the decision model and adaptive one-question interview UX, directed the WebMCP workflow and tool contract, integrated the shared local-first store with the Next.js/TypeScript UI, and coordinated implementation and review. I deployed the Vercel demo, validated the browser workflow, created demo fixtures and documentation, and prepared the video and submission materials. AI coding tools supported implementation, but the product decisions, architecture, testing, and final integration were my responsibility.
